answer: The pigment multiplier is published, charged in vertex, and pulse lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2225 identities would post 3570 proofs and burn roughly 34 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
